title: Geliyo musun?
goal: Understand and use the spoken present continuous and future, and write them in standard spelling when it matters.

intro.text: In speech the r of `-(I)yor` drops: *geliyo*, *biliyo musun*, *napıyosun*; with *ben*, *geliyorum* sounds like *geliyom*. The future shrinks too: *geleceğim* becomes *gelicem* or *gelcem*, *yapacağız* becomes *yapıcaz*. Use these with friends, and write the standard everywhere else.

vocab.en: What are you doing?; What's up? (spoken: Ne yapıyorsun?)
What did you do?; How did it go? (spoken: Ne yaptın?)
What are you going to do? (spoken: Ne yapacaksın?)
What are you saying?; What do you think? (spoken: Ne diyorsun?)
Listen, there's something I want to tell you. (spoken: Bir şey diyeceğim.)
to write to each other; to text each other

exercises.question: Your friend texts *Bugün gelmiyom.* What does she mean?

why.2: That would be *gelemiyom*, with the `-(y)AmA` of inability.

exercises.explain: *Gelmiyom* is *gelmiyorum* as it is said: the present continuous, negative, with *-yorum* shrunk to *-yom*.

exercises.label: *gelmek* in the present continuous as people say it: *geliyom*, …

accept: geliyom
geliyosun
geliyon
geliyo
geliyoruz
geliyoz
geliyosunuz
geliyonuz
geliyolar
geliyo

exercises.explain: The r of `-(I)yor` drops before a consonant and at the end of the word: *geliyo*, *geliyosun*, *geliyolar*. With *ben*, *-yorum* shrinks to *-yom*; with *biz*, a vowel follows and the r usually stays.

exercises.en: Are you coming to the cinema tomorrow?

accept: geliyor

reject.why: That's how it sounds. In standard spelling, `-(I)yor` keeps its r: *geliyor musun?*

exercises.hint: Your friend said *geliyo musun?* Write it in standard spelling.
exercises.explain: In writing, `-(I)yor` keeps its r, and the question particle stays a separate word: *geliyor musun?*

accept: What are you saying? I do not understand at all.
What are you saying? I do not understand it at all.
What are you talking about? I do not understand (it) at all.
What are you on about? I do not understand (it) at all.
What are you [saying|talking about|on about]? I do not understand [a thing|anything|a word].
exercises.explain: *Diyosun* is *diyorsun* and *anlamıyom* is *anlamıyorum*. *Sen* after the verb adds a note of reproach.

exercises.question: *Akşam yediye kadar işteyim, sonra gelicem.* What is *gelicem* in standard spelling?

why.1: *Gelirim* is the aorist; in speech it stays *gelirim*.

exercises.explain: The future narrows its vowel and drops ğ in speech: *geleceğim* → *gelicem*.

exercises.text: — Bu akşam ___? — Bilmiyom, evde kalıcam herhâlde.
exercises.en: What are you doing tonight? — Dunno, I'll probably stay in.
exercises.explain: *Napıcan* is *ne yapacaksın*: a question about the evening ahead, answered with *kalıcam* (*kalacağım*). *Naptın* (what did you do?) and *napıyodun* (what were you doing?) look back.

exercises.prompt: Yarın erken kalkıcaz, sabah altıda yola çıkıcaz.
accept: We will get up early tomorrow and set off at six in the morning.
We will get up early tomorrow and set off at 6 in the morning.
We will get up early tomorrow and leave at [six|6] in the morning.
We will get up early tomorrow and head off at [six|6] in the morning.
We will get up early tomorrow and hit the road at [six|6] in the morning.
We are going to get up early tomorrow and [set off|leave|head off|hit the road] at [six|6] in the morning.
Tomorrow we [will|are going to] get up early and [set off|leave|head off|hit the road] at [six|6] in the morning.
We [will|are going to] get up early tomorrow; we [will|are going to] [set off|leave|head off|hit the road] at [six|6] in the morning.
exercises.explain: *Kalkıcaz* and *çıkıcaz* are *kalkacağız* and *çıkacağız*: the vowel narrows to ı, and ğ with the vowel after it falls away.

exercises.question: Which sentence would you write in an email to your landlord?

why.1: Spoken spelling: fine with a friend, too casual for a landlord.
why.2: The fastest spoken form: only for close friends.

exercises.explain: In an email to someone you don't know well, write the standard future: *geleceğim*.

accept: anlatacağım

reject.why: Correct Turkish, but *anlatıcam* is the future: *anlatacağım*.

exercises.hint: Your friend said *anlatıcam*. Write it in standard spelling.
exercises.explain: *Anlatıcam* is the spoken *anlatacağım*: the a of `-AcAk` narrows to ı, and *-ğım* becomes *-m*.

exercises.title: Kardeşimle yazışma
exercises.passage:
**Elif:** Napıyosun? Akşama geliyo musun?

**Can:** Bilmiyom ya, çok işim var. Belki geç gelicem.

**Elif:** Annem seni soruyo. Börek yapıyomuş, senin için.

**Can:** Gerçekten mi? Tamam o zaman, yedide oradayım. Ekmek alayım mı?

**Elif:** Al, al. Bir de tatlı alırsan süper olur.

**Can:** Tamam, alırım. Görüşürüz!
exercises.translation: Elif: What are you up to? Are you coming this evening? Can: I don't know, I've got a lot of work. Maybe I'll come late. Elif: Mum's asking about you. She's making börek, apparently, for you. Can: Really? OK then, I'll be there at seven. Shall I get bread? Elif: Yes, do. And if you get a dessert too, that'd be great. Can: OK, I will. See you!

options: He doesn't know: he has a lot of work
questions.explain: *Bilmiyom ya, çok işim var. Belki geç gelicem.* He decides on seven only later.

questions.q: Why does Elif say *yapıyomuş* rather than *yapıyo*?
options: She is passing on what her mother told her
She saw her mother making it
It is a guess about the future
questions.explain: *Yapıyomuş* is *yapıyormuş*: `-(y)mIş` on a tense passes on what you were told ([B1 unit 12](gp-reported-mis)).

questions.q: How is *soruyo* written in standard Turkish?
questions.explain: The r of `-(I)yor` drops at the end of the word in speech: *soruyor* → *soruyo*.
